Food-food.read.description:
What a food is, shared by every household: nutrition per 100 g, allergens, food groups, spice,
and how much a piece or a millilitre weighs (docs/INGREDIENT-KNOWLEDGE.md). One per canonical
key; a household's Ingredient points at one, and can be pointed at another by hand. Filled in
by the text model (DescribeFoodsHandler); a fix made by hand is kept for good.

sourceRef.description: Where in `source` the figures come from ("2191 Garbanzo, en conserva" in BEDCA).

estimatedFields.description: nutrition fields `source` doesn't give, still the model's estimate

edited.description: Changed by hand: the model leaves it alone.

diet.description: The strictest diet it suits (vegan, vegetarian, pescatarian); null for meat, or while undescribed.

substitutesByName.description: Who chose the substitutes by hand, by name.

correctedByName.description: Who fixed it by hand, by name.

Ingredient-ingredient.read.description:
The household's catalog of ingredients, one per canonical key ("onion", whatever the recipe
language), so a shopping list can merge them, name them in each viewer's language and put
them in the right aisle (docs/PLAN.md §7). New ones are classified by the text model
(ClassifyIngredientsHandler); a fix made in the app is kept for good. Each points at the shared
Food with the same key (nutrition, allergens…), or at another one chosen by hand.

staple.description: Always in the kitchen (salt, oil…): listed apart, to check rather than buy.

food.description: What it is, nutritionally: the food with the same key when it was added, or another one set by hand.

recipeCount.description: Not stored: how many of the household's recipes use it (IngredientProvider).

MealPlan-meal_plan.read_recipe.list.description:
A week's lunches and dinners (docs/PLAN.md §6). Weeks start on Monday. Each planned meal is an
entry; a meal that isn't planned (eating out) has none. Every action answers with the whole
plan, so the app redraws the week from one response.

leftovers.description: Cook dinner for two meals: the next day's lunch is its leftovers.

weekdayMaxMinutes.description: Longest recipe (prep + cook) for Monday to Friday; null for no limit.

tweak.description: A wish for this week only ("my mother comes: no pork"), as the household wrote it; null without one.

tweakAvoids.description:
Recipes the week's rules have something against, when the wish was read: the app leaves
them out of its swap suggestions this week.

MealPlan.MealPlanEntryAction.description: Pick another recipe for one meal.

rating.description: How it turned out (1-5): rates the meal and its recipe.

recipe.description: Id of a library recipe to cook for this meal.

leftoverOf.description: Make it the leftovers of another meal of the plan, with the same recipe (undoing "No lo hicimos").

cooked.description:
Cooked (true), not cooked (false), or back to nobody has said (null). Left uninitialised
when the request doesn't send it, as null is a value here (undoing "No lo hicimos").

MealPlan.MealPlanEntryRestore.description: Put back a meal taken off the menu, as it was and linked to its leftovers (undo).

reasons.description: Why the planner chose it, as the plan gave it.

leftoverOf.description: The meal it was the leftovers of.

ShareToken-share_token.read.description:
A personal token that lets one device save links without a session: the iPhone Shortcut
sends it to POST /api/share (ShareController). Only its SHA-256 hash is stored; the token

tags.description:
What the household's AI calls have cost (extracting links, sorting ingredients), in USD at
list price (config/services.yaml app.llm_prices). Months are calendar months in UTC.

tags.description: The signed-in user and their household: what the SPA needs to boot.

tags.name: Password
tags.description:
Forgotten passwords, for people who aren't signed in (changing it while signed in is
POST /api/me/password). See App\Security\PasswordReset.

tags.name: RecipeSearchResult
tags.description: A library recipe found by meaning (App\Search\RecipeSearch), and how close it is.

tags.name: RecipeTag
tags.description: A tag used in the household's library and how many recipes carry it: the library's filter chips.

tags.name: ShoppingList
tags.description:
A week's shopping list (see App\Shopping\ShoppingListBuilder). Every action answers with the
whole list. Lines are identified by `key`: the ingredient key, or "item:<id>" for items
added by hand.

tags.name: SimilarRecipe
tags.description: A library recipe like another one ("more like this", App\Library\Similarity), and what they share.

tags.name: SwapFeedback
tags.description: Why a planned meal was swapped (App\Entity\SwapFeedback): what the household's swaps teach.

tags.name: TasteProfile
tags.description:
What the household likes (docs/PLAN.md §6.1): the questionnaire's answers, the rules the
planner follows, the notes and summary, and what the rules do to the library. 404 until the
household has said.

tags.name: Food
tags.description:
What a food is, shared by every household: nutrition per 100 g, allergens, food groups, spice,
and how much a piece or a millilitre weighs (docs/INGREDIENT-KNOWLEDGE.md). One per canonical
key; a household's Ingredient points at one, and can be pointed at another by hand. Filled in
by the text model (DescribeFoodsHandler); a fix made by hand is kept for good.

tags.name: Ingredient
tags.description:
The household's catalog of ingredients, one per canonical key ("onion", whatever the recipe
language), so a shopping list can merge them, name them in each viewer's language and put
them in the right aisle (docs/PLAN.md §7). New ones are classified by the text model
(ClassifyIngredientsHandler); a fix made in the app is kept for good. Each points at the shared
Food with the same key (nutrition, allergens…), or at another one chosen by hand.

tags.name: MealPlan
tags.description:
A week's lunches and dinners (docs/PLAN.md §6). Weeks start on Monday. Each planned meal is an
entry; a meal that isn't planned (eating out) has none. Every action answers with the whole
plan, so the app redraws the week from one response.
